newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus politician rushed to hospital.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus politician rushed to hospital.

text.p: Greek Cypriot politician Yiannakis Matsis, chairman of the largest Cyprus party, was rushed to hospital on Wednesday night after suffering a heart attack, doctors said.
Matsis, 63, president of the right-wing Democratic Rally party, was taken to a hospital in the western coastal town of Paphos, where doctors said he had suffered a mild heart attack.
He collapsed immediately after a party conference in the town, witnesses said.
Matsis assumed the leadership of the Rally party in 1993 after its founder, Glafcos Clerides, was elected president of the republic.
He recently weathered a storm in his party after several members insisted on standing as independent candidates in forthcoming municipal elections without the party's consent.
Health Minister Manolis Christofides and Cypriot heart surgeon Costakis Zambartas flew to Paphos from the capital Nicosia in a police helicopter to be briefed on Matsis' conditon.
